title: Quant profile orchestration: INT8/FP8 switchboard and empirical validation for Hopper
creator: Oliver Grant
description:
Problem: We need a safe, observable mechanism to enable FP8 on Hopper (E4M3/E5M2) across our model catalog while providing an automated INT8 fallback when FP8 produces measurable quality regressions. Current efforts have separate calibration pipelines and heuristics; this ticket builds a runtime switchboard + validation harness that orchestrates profile selection (E4M3 vs E5M2), enforces safety gates, and performs empirical cross-model validation before and during rollout.

Scope:
- Implement a 'quant-profile switchboard' service that chooses active quantization profile per model & workload (based on model family, sequence-length, and distributional telemetry).
- Add automated INT8 fallback path that can be invoked at runtime if FP8 drift or quality regressions are detected.
- Standardize calibration artifact format (scale tables, outlier stats, per-layer histograms) so the runtime and CI harness can consume the same artifacts.
- Create an offline empirical validation harness to run acceptance tests across a curated cross-section of internal and public prompts (LLMs, chat, instruction-following, long-context summarization).
- Define acceptance/rejection thresholds and integrate them into canary gating.

Why this differs from previous work: Previous tickets tackled calibration pipelines and single-model activation heuristics. Here we focus on orchestration and the dynamic decisioning needed in production (runtime switches, live fallback, and cross-model validation with strict pass/fail criteria).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Switchboard service deployed in staging and able to route requests to FP8-E4M3, FP8-E5M2, and INT8 variants based on configuration.
2) Offline validation harness can run a 50-model matrix (varying sizes, token lengths, batch sizes) within 6 hours and emit a pass/fail report.
3) Canary rollout plan defined with 5% traffic gate, automated rollback on regression, and documented rollback thresholds.
4) Telemetry signals (LLR drop, sample perplexity delta, top-k token distribution shift) wired into the alerting dashboard.
5) Integration tests that simulate KV-cache misalignment and confirm fallback path preserves correctness.
6) PRs merged for switchboard, artifacts format, and validation harness.
rollout_plan:
Stage 1: Staging-only validation (manual runs) using the harness; ensure stable PRs and artifacts.
Stage 2: Internal canary (10 internal teams) at 1% traffic for 48h; monitor telemetry.
Stage 3: Public canary at 5% traffic, 72h, automated rollback.
Stage 4: Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with progressive expansion of model families.
Fallback: Immediate runtime fallback to INT8 if any of the hard thresholds trigger; manual inspection required before re-enabling FP8 for that model.
Communication: Postmortem and rollout notes published to #infra-quant and a Confluence page linked below.
test_plan:
Offline: run the harness across a curated set of ~50 models (small, medium, large) sampling three sequence lengths (128, 1024, 8192) and two batch profiles. Report metrics: token-likelihood delta, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, embedding cosine drift, and API error rates.
Integration: simulate burst traffic and KV-cache warmup to validate no OOB reads on kernel switch.
Canary: traffic split 95/5 with logging of per-request chosen profile, latency p95, and token-quality metrics.
Acceptance thresholds: mean token-likelihood drop < 0.8% and 95th percentile latency increase < 15ms for the same hardware profile. If token-likelihood drop > 1.5% or embedding drift > 2.0%, auto rollback triggers.
telemetry_signals:
- token_likelihood_delta (per-profile baseline)
- perplexity_delta
- embedding_cosine_drift
- inference_error_rate (exceptions, NaNs)
- p50/p95 latency per-profile
- kernel_recompile_counts
- kv_cache_misalignments_detected
- profile_switch_rate
comments:
2025-02-18 - Oliver Grant: Kickoff. Spun up initial repo for switchboard (WIP). Collected stakeholder requirements from serving, infra, and QA. Assigned to Maya for implementation. Links to existing calibration artifacts attached.

Decision: we will support both E4M3 and E5M2 profiles and defer automatic profile selection ML model to a follow-up; initial heuristics will be rules-based (model family + seq len).

2025-02-24 - Maya Chen: Completed prototype of artifact schema and adapter; artifacts now include per-layer scale, outlier-percentiles, and activation histograms. Ran quick pass with LLaMA2-13B on E4M3 and observed small decoder head instability at long context > 6k tokens. Opened PR #4718 with tests.

2025-02-26 - QA (Priya Nair): Validation harness added 25 baseline prompts and 10 failure-mode prompts (adversarial numerics). Observed two regressions on abstractive summarization for FP8-E5M2 with greedy decoding; example attached in Confluence. Marking as blocker until we identify root cause.

2025-02-28 - Maya Chen: Root cause narrowed to dynamic range clipping in layernorm after quantized matmul on E5M2 kernels at long contexts. Implemented a conservative clip and re-ran harness: regressions reduced but not eliminated. Next: introduce per-layer bias-correction calibration step in the offline pipeline.

2025-03-02 - Infra (Liam O'Connor): Added telemetry hooks for kv_cache_misalignments and kernel_recompile_counts. Also created a temporary canary route in staging to exercise fallback path (fp8->int8) and verified requests successfully route to INT8 runtime. Latency delta acceptable in staging.

2025-03-04 - Maya Chen: Implemented INT8 runtime fallback and unit tests simulating jitter and misaligned KV cache. Preparing canary run playbook. Need approval from SRE and Product for customer-impact thresholds. Requesting review from Oliver and Priya before scheduling internal canary.
